title: Journal entry_price is the package's planned entry, not the fill: write the actual entry fill back so computed P&L and every R / entry-based analysis use the real entry
clears_when: new closes carry the entry fill from the venue, the readers named in scope use it, and the 30d bias measurement says which historic R figures are distorted
note:
EVIDENCE 2026-11-14 (manager GO 17:59Z): raw Bybit closed-pnl records vs journal rows. SOL: venue avg_entry 73.60 (bybit_portfolio 7224) and 73.58 (bybit_2 7223) vs journal entry_price 73.85. XRP: 0.9707 (bybit_2 7226) vs 0.9715. Proof on 7224: (71.9-73.60) x 471.1 - fee 37.70 = -838.57 = the venue closed_pnl to the cent. Real money: bybit_2 7223 entry off 0.37%. So pnl_computed, R and every entry-based analysis on these rows use an entry that was never filled. SCOPE FIRST: (1) per venue, is the entry fill (avg price, qty) available at order confirmation or from a fills read (Bybit execution list, Alpaca filled_avg_price, IB execDetails, prop terminals)? (2) where to write it: a NEW entry_fill_price column is safer for history than overwriting entry_price (consumers read entry_price as the plan, e.g. bracket R); (3) which readers switch to the fill (net_r_label, R figures, live review, local_pnl). Pairs with the 30d bias measurement ENTRY-FILL-BIAS-30D. Scope input from ENTRY-FILL-BIAS-30D (2026-11-15, PR #26166): (1) on real-money/portfolio clean rows the plan-vs-fill gap is small on average (mean R bias <= 0.003R) but p90 ~25 bps, with 7/44 rows over 0.05R; (2) on overlapping rows, notably bybit_1 netting (160/164), Bybit closed-pnl gives the POSITION average, so the write-back must read the entry order's own fill (Bybit execution list by orderId, broker_order_id), not closed-pnl; (3) 16/27 alpaca_paper broker_order_ids are not_found at Alpaca, so check what id is stored before relying on it for filled_avg_price; (4) IB needs an execDetails read (none exists in diag). SCOPE (AM-OPS 2026-11-15 ~01:15Z, code read of src/units/accounts/execute.py at origin/main):
(1) ALPACA ALREADY DONE: since ALPACA-LIVE-MECHANICS (2026-11-06), _log_trade_to_journal books order['venue_fill'].avg_price (AlpacaClient.place's confirm-poll avgPrice) as entry_price, keeps the plan in notes.package_entry, and sets notes.entry_price_source (execute.py ~1333-1347 and ~2693-2706). This matches the measured alpaca_paper bias of ~0 on the rows it could read.
(2) BYBIT: placement returns only orderId, and nothing reads the fill back. A read-back helper of the right shape already exists for reduces: read_reduce_fill (~2123, get_open_orders / get_order_history by orderId, never raises, 3 attempts x 0.25 s). It runs ON the order path.
(3) IB: ib_client exposes avgFillPrice on order status (~4533); not wired to the journal.
(4) PRECEDENT for WHERE: Alpaca OVERWRITES entry_price with the fill and keeps the plan in notes. The row's original suggestion (a new entry_fill_price column) would diverge from that precedent; following the precedent keeps one meaning per venue but changes what R readers see.
PROPOSED DESIGN (for the build, Tier 2): an OFF-order-path sweep in order_monitor reads each new open Bybit (then IB) trade's entry order by orderId (broker_order_id) once, takes avgPrice/cumExecQty, and writes it back with the same notes keys as Alpaca (entry_price_source=bybit_order_history, package_entry). It adds no latency at entry: one read per new trade, from the sweep. DECISION NEEDED from the manager/operator before building: overwrite entry_price (the Alpaca precedent) or add entry_fill_price (the row's original suggestion)? Readers that compute R (net_r_label, conflicting_exposure, live review) would follow either. DECISION (Manager Session 2026-11-14a, 00:51Z): option (a). OVERWRITE entry_price with the entry fill and keep the plan in notes.package_entry (the Alpaca precedent). Reasons: one meaning of entry_price across venues; the plan is preserved; R readers need no per-venue switch. Conditions: (1) the entry order's own avgPrice by orderId, never a position average; unisolable -> plan + reason; (2) a DB field update only, no bracket side effects; (3) entry_price_source on every row; (4) no backfill. BUILT 2026-11-15 ~01:30Z: PR #26167 (draft, Tier-2 hold, restart batch), 13 tests pinning each condition. Clears when the first new Bybit entry after deploy reads entry_price_source=bybit_order_history with entry_price = the venue order avgPrice and package_entry = the plan. Separately filed: 16/27 alpaca_paper broker_order_ids not_found at Alpaca (ENTRY-FILL-BIAS-30D). 2026-11-15 02:32Z: #26167 merged (with #26163, one restart batch). landed_unproven. Clears on: (a) trader restart onto the merge with all positions accounted for; (b) the first new Bybit entry after deploy reads notes.entry_price_source=bybit_order_history, entry_price = the venue order avgPrice, package_entry = the plan; (c) no SL/TP change on that trade from the writeback. Post-deploy 02:51Z (5682c699 deployed at the 02:38Z restart). There have been no new trades since the restart; the newest is id 7249 at 00:03:59Z, so nothing exercises the writeback yet. journalctl since boot: 0 matches for entry_fill_writeback (that scan hit its time budget, so the 0 is a lower bound) and 0 for _sweep_entry_fill_writeback (scan complete). Not an error; there is no input yet. Re-check after the 04:00Z 4h close (scheduled 04:15Z). Still landed_unproven: merged and deployed, NOT observed.
